supporting_observations.claim: The closest console-related process records in the supplied evidence show conhost.exe running as SYSTEM at 14:12:25, launched by csrss.exe, and exiting about one second later. They do not show PowerShell, and this activity is later than the reported time of around 13:40.

At 13:44, the workstation used the proxy to download from download.windowsupdate.com with a Windows Update Agent user agent. This records update-related network activity but does not identify a PowerShell process or explain the reported window.
The supplied records do not establish that the reported PowerShell window was malicious or benign; neither the reported process nor its command line and parent process are shown for around 13:40.

known_telemetry_limitations: The supplied evidence does not include PowerShell-specific events or process-creation records for the reported time around 13:40. The available console-related process records are for conhost.exe at 14:12 (T024-00285 through T024-00288), so this excerpt cannot establish what appeared on screen around 13:40.
The supplied records do not include PowerShell script-block or module logging, a transcript, or a complete endpoint process tree for the alert window.
claims_not_established: Whether PowerShell actually executed on WS-MLOPEZ-01 around 13:40, and if so, its command line, parent process, user context, and actions.
Whether the reported window was caused by an authorized task, an interactive action, or malicious activity.
Whether the 13:44 Windows Update traffic was related to the reported window.
